title: Wildfire survivor health study findings
summary: The Maui Wildfire Exposure Cohort Study told a committee recovery is uneven, with about 23 percent of participants still severely food insecure, many in temporary housing, and children's low self-esteem rising from about 13 to 26 percent. The study plans to serve 1,000 more residents through Hoʻala starting in January and said the parks department would not let it use parks for screenings.

timeline.text: A researcher said the share of participants with poor lung function rose about 5%, for reasons not yet known.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Researchers asked council members to help find schools, churches, community centers and housing sites for free screenings.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Among children, low self-esteem rose from about 13% to 26%.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Researchers hope to serve 1,000 more residents, mainly children, through a program called Hoʻala starting in January.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: About 23% of participants remain severely food insecure, which researchers said is unchanged.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Among adults who came back for follow-up, employment rose from 62% to nearly 81%.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The study has completed more than 4,000 appointments involving over 2,500 children and adults since January 2024.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Researchers updated the committee on a study that has tracked survivors' health for three years after the Maui wildfires.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Temporary housing among adults in the wildfire study fell from about 4 in 10 to about 3 in 10.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The team said the parks department would not let them use parks because they collect blood from adults.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Researchers said recovery is underway but uneven.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The committee received an update on the Maui Wildfire Exposure Cohort Study, a health study of wildfire survivors.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee
